text:
ravi-devex: Quick note — while updating the next-llamaindex-starter sample I hit SDK parity and auth quirks. Posting reproduce + proposed short fixes.

ella-frontend: TL;DR?

ravi-devex: Two issues: 1) SDK retry behavior differs between node/browser builds (browser abandons on 401). 2) Eval harness fails when streaming embeddings + chat in the same page — looks like a shared fetch/agent race.

noah-ml: Can you paste minimal repros?

ravi-devex: Minimal JS from sample: 
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: RW_KEY, retry: { retries: 1 } });
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood/embed-small', input });
await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood/chat-mini', input });
```
Locally with ephemeral dev tokens the embeddings call returns 401 then 200, browser SDK surfaces error and stops. Python SDK retries once. Also when both requests run on the same page the eval harness sometimes deadlocks waiting for second stream.

ella-frontend: Deadlock? Is it promise ordering or shared body reader?

ravi-devex: Looks like our browser bundler replaced the low-level fetch wrapper with a polyfill that uses a global ReadableStream helper. When two streams start simultaneously the helper collapses chunks into one reader and the chat stream never yields EOF so the pump hangs.

noah-ml: Sounds like two fixes: enable optional authRetry for browser SDK; and in sample avoid concurrent live streaming of embeddings + chat by sequencing or cloning the response.

ivy-docs: For onboarding we want minimal confusion. Recommended changes for the sample: - set retry: { retries: 1, authRetry: true } in client init (comment why) - run embeddings first, await completion, then start chat stream - add a short section in README called "Known dev token race" with the workaround.

ravi-devex: I added a tiny helper in the sample to serialize streaming calls for now. Patch will include tests that mock 401->200 and concurrent streams.

ella-frontend: Can we also expose `client.stream({ raw: true })` so sample can use a conservative reader shim? That avoids altering default SDK semantics.

noah-ml: Agree. SDK change should be opt-in flags only. We can ship `authRetry` and `stream.raw` as opt-ins in a patch and flip defaults later after telemetry.

ci-bot: [ci] job 6120: examples/next-llamaindex-starter smoke test queued

ivy-docs: I'll update README and include a small troubleshooting FAQ for new users who hit token races or streaming quirks on Vercel Edge.

ravi-devex: I'll open two tiny PRs: INF-6200 (sample sequencing + docs) and INF-6201 (SDK opt-in flags + tests). Pinged reviewers. Thanks all :pray:
